title: Hero support and transit: HoMM3 to Aurelion Reach
scope: General hero-support, learning, scouting, information, faction landmarks, route-control, sea-travel and small weekly support producers. Archived campaign/scenario-only sites, mines, creature dwellings, treasure pickups and creature banks are outside this reference.
evidence_boundary: H3MapEd supplies object identities, placements and native connection data; the original game's executable supplies visit effects. The original-effect column summarizes standard HoMM3 behavior using the original 1999 manual and pinned VCMI compatibility sources. VCMI is an independent implementation, not recovered H3MapEd source. Our mapping column is inspected from the current C++ adapter. This reference makes no new native-generator parity claim.

original_types.name: Altar of Sacrifice
original_types.effect: Exchange creatures or artifacts for hero experience, subject to hero alignment.
original_types.difference: No dedicated sacrifice visit is selected by this resolver. Source eligibility classifies type 2 as guarded_reward, so it does not enter the generic interactable-site fallback either.

original_types.name: Arena
original_types.effect: Choose a permanent +2 Attack or +2 Defense, once per hero.
original_types.difference: The original stat-choice role is retained with our content and art.

original_types.name: Black Market
original_types.effect: Buy from a selection of artifacts for resources.
original_types.difference: No black-market artifact shop is selected; a generic visit building is substituted.

original_types.name: Boat
original_types.effect: Board a vessel to travel over water; embarkation/disembarkation consume the day's movement in standard HoMM3.
original_types.difference: Boat records are skipped by the resource-site adapter. Sailing is a separate WaterTravelRules system, not a claimable support building.

original_types.name: Border Guard
original_types.effect: A matching-colour Keymaster Tent authorizes removal of the barrier.
original_types.difference: Translated to a terrain-selected paid/unlock gate; the original colour-key requirement is not implemented by this mapping.

original_types.name: Keymaster Tent
original_types.effect: Records a player's visit to the tent colour, authorizing matching guards and gates.
original_types.difference: Explicitly skipped by GeneratedRewardRules; no key-collection support site is adopted by that resolver.

original_types.name: Buoy
original_types.effect: +1 morale for the next battle.
original_types.difference: Becomes a weekly hero visit granting our cohesion bonus.

original_types.name: Cartographer
original_types.effect: Pay 1,000 gold to reveal water, land or underground according to the cartographer subtype; information is shared by the player.
original_types.difference: Our Chartmaker reveals its current map level; the H3 subtype-specific reveal distinction is collapsed.

original_types.name: Swan Pond
original_types.effect: +2 luck for the next battle and lose remaining movement.
original_types.difference: Becomes a weekly Fortune Ring; the movement loss and +2 luck effect are not preserved.

original_types.name: Cover of Darkness
original_types.effect: Re-shrouds a surrounding area for opponents.
original_types.difference: Generic visit-building substitution; the original re-shrouding effect is absent from this translation.

original_types.name: Marletto Tower
original_types.effect: Permanent +1 Defense, once per hero.
original_types.difference: Retains the defense-training role.

original_types.name: Eye of the Magi
original_types.effect: An eye provides remote revealed areas when the matching Hut of the Magi is visited.
original_types.difference: Becomes a local 12-tile survey visit; the Hut-to-Eye remote network is not preserved.

original_types.name: Faerie Ring
original_types.effect: +1 luck for the next battle.
original_types.difference: Translated into our weekly momentum visit.

original_types.name: Fountain of Fortune
original_types.effect: A weekly roll gives -1, +1, +2 or +3 luck for the next battle.
original_types.difference: Our generated override rolls positive momentum +1 to +3; the negative outcome is omitted.

original_types.name: Fountain of Youth
original_types.effect: +400 movement points and +1 morale for the next battle.
original_types.difference: Our Wayside Rest grants 4 movement and +1 cohesion, with a weekly-per-hero limit. Movement units differ between games.

original_types.name: Garden of Revelation
original_types.effect: Permanent +1 Knowledge, once per hero.
original_types.difference: Retains the knowledge-training role.

original_types.name: Garrison — horizontal
original_types.effect: An army guards passage; ownership and whether troops may be removed control interaction. Anti-magic variants restrict battle spells.
original_types.difference: Gate interaction is rethemed through the paid/unlock pool. Do not infer an original garrison troop-transfer or anti-magic interface from the new site name.

original_types.name: Hill Fort
original_types.effect: Upgrade existing creatures, with tier-dependent discounts; first-level upgrades are free.
original_types.difference: No Hill Fort upgrading interface is selected; the adapter substitutes a generic visit building.

original_types.name: Hut of the Magi
original_types.effect: Reveals the areas around Eyes of the Magi.
original_types.difference: Translated to the same local Lens Calibration Cart as an Eye; the remote-eye system is lost.

original_types.name: Idol of Fortune
original_types.effect: Odd weekdays give +1 luck, even weekdays +1 morale; day seven gives both, for the next battle.
original_types.difference: Our Fortune Ring grants weekly momentum without the weekday-dependent morale/luck distinction.

original_types.name: Library of Enlightenment
original_types.effect: +2 to all four primary skills once per hero; normally requires level 10, with lower level thresholds through Diplomacy.
original_types.difference: Grand Archive grants the same four stat gains but has a fixed level-10 requirement.

original_types.name: Lighthouse
original_types.effect: Ownership grants the player's heroes +500 sea-movement points.
original_types.difference: Any of seven scouting structures can replace it. Their held-vision effects do not reproduce the original sea-movement bonus.

original_types.name: Monolith One-Way Entrance
original_types.effect: Teleports a visiting hero to an exit in the matching channel.
original_types.difference: Uses the native channel and destination records; Waygate is the entrance name. Native transit bypasses generic claiming and local-route effects.

original_types.name: Monolith One-Way Exit
original_types.effect: Receives travellers from the matching entrance; it is not a return entrance.
original_types.difference: Wayfall is arrival-only. Its portal-network role is authoritative.

original_types.name: Monolith Two-Way
original_types.effect: Travel between monoliths in a matching channel; several matching destinations can exist.
original_types.difference: Wayring uses native destination groups, with random selection among valid exits when appropriate.

original_types.name: School of Magic
original_types.effect: Pay 1,000 gold for permanent +1 Spell Power or +1 Knowledge, once per hero.
original_types.difference: Retains the paid choice using our power/knowledge stats.

original_types.name: Magic Spring
original_types.effect: Refill spell points to 200% of normal maximum; visiting capacity resets weekly.
original_types.difference: Moonspring uses our week_double mana effect with a weekly-site visit limit. Original active-tile behavior is not represented as two separate uses here.

original_types.name: Magic Well
original_types.effect: Refill spell points to normal maximum, at most once that day for a hero.
original_types.difference: Ley Well retains daily-per-hero mana restoration.

original_types.name: Mercenary Camp
original_types.effect: Permanent +1 Attack, once per hero.
original_types.difference: Retains the attack-training role.

original_types.name: Mermaids
original_types.effect: +1 luck for the next battle.
original_types.difference: Translated to our weekly Fortune Ring and momentum.

original_types.name: Mystical Garden
original_types.effect: Once weekly, yields either 500 gold or 5 gems.
original_types.difference: Our Orchard Levy Post pays fixed gold with a seven-day cooldown.

original_types.name: Oasis
original_types.effect: +800 movement points and +1 morale for the next battle.
original_types.difference: Shares Wayside Rest with Fountain of Youth, so its larger original movement award is lost.

original_types.name: Obelisk
original_types.effect: Reveals another portion of the Grail-location puzzle map.
original_types.difference: Can become any of nine faction landmarks. A Grail-puzzle visit is replaced by vision/control and, on six variants, timed town support and unpaid troop dispatch.

original_types.name: Redwood Observatory
original_types.effect: Reveals a radius of 20 tiles around the location.
original_types.difference: Becomes one of seven capturable scouting variants, each with radius 18, rather than the original 20-tile reveal.

original_types.name: Ocean Bottle
original_types.effect: Displays the map author's message and is collected.
original_types.difference: Converted to a sign-waypoint pool; do not infer preservation of the original bottle message or removal cadence.

original_types.name: Pillar of Fire
original_types.effect: Reveals a radius of 20 tiles around the location.
original_types.difference: Shares the radius-18 scouting pool with Lighthouse and Redwood Observatory.

original_types.name: Star Axis
original_types.effect: Permanent +1 Spell Power, once per hero.
original_types.difference: Retains the power-training role.

original_types.name: Prison
original_types.effect: Frees the imprisoned hero to join the visiting player's side.
original_types.difference: Captive Stockade frees one available commander of the visiting faction at level one, with a starting army, once per placement. This reworks the original map-configured prisoner. No hire fee; four-command cap and legal adjacent spawning still apply.

original_types.name: Rally Flag
original_types.effect: +400 movement points, +1 morale and +1 luck for the next battle.
original_types.difference: Muster Banner uses 2 movement, +1 cohesion and +1 momentum, once per hero per week.

original_types.name: Sanctuary
original_types.effect: A hero occupying the sanctuary cannot be attacked.
original_types.difference: Generic visit-building substitution does not provide the original occupation protection.

original_types.name: Scholar
original_types.effect: One-use teaching of a primary skill, secondary skill or spell; the scholar disappears.
original_types.difference: One of six learning sites is chosen instead; original reward kind and disappearance are not preserved.

original_types.name: Seer's Hut
original_types.effect: Offers a configured quest and its reward.
original_types.difference: A generic visit-building fallback is selected, not the original quest system.

original_types.name: Shipyard
original_types.effect: Build a boat for 1,000 gold and 10 wood at a usable launch position.
original_types.difference: Our repeatable shipyard has the same nominal resource cost and validates a usable launch tile.

original_types.name: Shrine of Magic Incantation — level 1
original_types.effect: Teach the shrine's level-1 spell to a hero able to learn it.
original_types.difference: Maps to our tier-1 shrine and spell pool; original spell content is replaced.

original_types.name: Shrine of Magic Gesture — level 2
original_types.effect: Teach the shrine's level-2 spell to a hero able to learn it.
original_types.difference: Maps to our tier-2 shrine and spell pool; original spell content is replaced.

original_types.name: Shrine of Magic Thought — level 3
original_types.effect: Teach the shrine's level-3 spell, subject to learning prerequisites.
original_types.difference: Maps to our tier-3 shrine. The games' learning prerequisites should not be assumed identical.

original_types.name: Sign
original_types.effect: Displays the map author's sign text.
original_types.difference: A themed sign from a five-site pool supplies our route-hint text.

original_types.name: Sirens
original_types.effect: Trade 30% of creatures in stacks for hero experience based on their hit points.
original_types.difference: A generic visit-building fallback replaces the sacrifice-for-experience behavior.

original_types.name: Stables
original_types.effect: +400 land movement for the week; Cavaliers can be upgraded to Champions free.
original_types.difference: Our Remount Stable grants +3 weekly movement; the Cavalier upgrade has no equivalent in this visit.

original_types.name: Tavern
original_types.effect: Hire heroes and obtain rumours.
original_types.difference: Wayfarer Lodge uses the existing shared weekly tavern roster and standard hero costs. Hire in the field without a town hall; the commander arrives beside the lodge. Four-command cap, unique heroes and current funds are enforced.

original_types.name: Temple
original_types.effect: +1 morale for the next battle; +2 on day seven.
original_types.difference: Wayside Chapel uses cohesion, with an additional day-seven bonus, and a weekly-per-hero limit.

original_types.name: Den of Thieves
original_types.effect: Provides extensive opponent and kingdom intelligence.
original_types.difference: Whisper Exchange gives a free visit-time kingdom report: army-strength ranking, towns, mines, commanders, creatures and gold. It also reveals town anchors/entrances across levels; both human and computer players can acquire the intelligence.

original_types.name: Trading Post
original_types.effect: Exchange resources at a fixed market efficiency.
original_types.difference: Wayside Exchange implements six fixed wood/ore/gold trades, not the full original resource market.

original_types.name: Learning Stone
original_types.effect: Gain 1,000 experience once per hero.
original_types.difference: Retains the experience award.

original_types.name: Tree of Knowledge
original_types.effect: Advance a level once per hero; the tree asks nothing, 2,000 gold or 10 gems according to its roll.
original_types.difference: Our level gain is retained; the 10-gem price becomes 10 of a selected Aurelion rare resource.

original_types.name: Subterranean Gate
original_types.effect: Travel between the surface and subterranean map through a paired gate.
original_types.difference: Basalt Undergate uses the recovered native peer/action-tile/level contract, ahead of generic transit-profile behavior.

original_types.name: University
original_types.effect: Pay to learn one of four offered secondary skills.
original_types.difference: A six-site learning pool replaces paid secondary-skill selection.

original_types.name: War Machine Factory
original_types.effect: Purchase war machines.
original_types.difference: No war-machine purchase interface is selected; the generic visit pool replaces it.

original_types.name: School of War
original_types.effect: Pay 1,000 gold for permanent +1 Attack or +1 Defense, once per hero.
original_types.difference: Retains the paid attack/defense choice.

original_types.name: Water Wheel
original_types.effect: Visit for 500 gold in week one, then 1,000 gold in later weeks.
original_types.difference: Chooses one of two Aurelion producers; inspect its configured reward and seven-day cooldown rather than assuming the original weekly gold schedule.

original_types.name: Watering Hole
original_types.effect: +400 movement points and +1 morale for the next battle.
original_types.difference: Cookfire Rest uses our 4-movement and cohesion effects, limited weekly per hero.

original_types.name: Whirlpool
original_types.effect: Teleport between whirlpools, normally losing half the weakest stack; original protection exceptions exist.
original_types.difference: Our weakest stack is selected by total stack HP; half its count is lost while keeping at least one creature in the whole army. A sailing hero is required.

original_types.name: Windmill
original_types.effect: Once weekly, collect 3–6 of a resource other than wood or gold.
original_types.difference: Chooses one of three producers. Wind Press gets a generated 3–6 rare-resource payload; other variants keep their configured payout.

original_types.name: Witch Hut
original_types.effect: Teach the hut's secondary skill at basic level, if the hero can learn it.
original_types.difference: Replaced by the six-site learning pool, not a retained secondary-skill hut.

original_types.name: Border Gate
original_types.effect: Requires a visit to the matching-colour Keymaster Tent; the gate remains.
original_types.difference: Shares the paid/unlock gate translation instead of colour-key authorization.

original_types.name: Freelancer's Guild
original_types.effect: Sell creatures for resources.
original_types.difference: No creature-selling interface is selected; the generic visit pool replaces it.

original_types.name: Quest Guard
original_types.effect: Blocks passage until its configured quest condition is fulfilled.
original_types.difference: Generic gate content replaces the original quest-condition semantics.

original_types.name: Garrison — vertical
original_types.effect: Vertical version of an army-guarded garrison; anti-magic variants exist.
original_types.difference: Shares the generic gate pool and its interaction, rather than an original garrison management interface.

original_types.name: Trading Post — alternate object type
original_types.effect: Alternate Trading Post object ID with the resource-exchange role.
original_types.difference: Maps to the same six fixed Wayside Exchange trades as type 99.
